hints: Differentiate $y = a x\mathrm{e}^{kx}$ using the product rule: $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = a\mathrm{e}^{kx} + akx\mathrm{e}^{kx} = a(1 + kx)\mathrm{e}^{kx}$.
Set $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = 0$. Since $a \neq 0$ and $\mathrm{e}^{kx} > 0$, deduce $1 + kx = 0 \implies x = -\frac{1}{k}$.
Substitute $k = -0.500$ to get $x = 2.00$.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate $y = a x \mathrm{e}^{k x}$ with respect to $x$ using the product rule:
$$\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = a(1)\mathrm{e}^{k x} + a x(k \mathrm{e}^{k x}) = a(1 + k x)\mathrm{e}^{k x}$$

Set the derivative to zero to find the stationary point:
$$a(1 + k x)\mathrm{e}^{k x} = 0$$
Since $a > 0$ and $\mathrm{e}^{k x} > 0$ for all real $x$, we have:
$$1 + k x = 0 \implies x = -\frac{1}{k} = -\frac{1}{-0.500} = 2.00$$

Evaluate the maximum value of $y$ at $x = 2.00$:
$$y_{\text{max}} = a(2.00)\mathrm{e}^{-0.500(2.00)} = 2 a \mathrm{e}^{-1} = 2(\mathrm{e}^{2.60})\mathrm{e}^{-1} = 2\mathrm{e}^{1.60}$$
$$y_{\text{max}} = 2(4.95303) \approx 9.90606 \implies y_{\text{max}} = 9.91$$

ai_rubric.observable: Applies product rule to differentiate $y = ax\mathrm{e}^{kx}$ to obtain $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = a(1 + kx)\mathrm{e}^{kx}$.
